statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 10% (low), Stress 64% (elevated), Confidence 79% (high).
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold because the observed Nasdaq-100 path is narrow and mean-reverting. Stress is elevated on live US-Iran escalation and a five-hour CME holiday halt. The only flagged window is the 22:00Z futures reopen, where Tail is mapped to WATCH for a single hour.
headline: Rangebound Labor Day tape; risk concentrated at the 22:00Z futures reopen
body: US cash equities are closed for Labor Day and CME equity-index futures halt at 17:00Z, resuming at 22:00Z. Into that halt NQ futures trade near 29,565 (+0.14%) inside a narrow 29,530-29,682 range, having faded about 117 points from the session high, so retracements are occurring and no one-way structure is present. VIX near 15.3 and a benign equity path contrast with a genuine energy and geopolitical impulse: Brent reached $97.93 and WTI about $92 after US strikes on three Iranian oil tankers, Iranian retaliation against vessels near the Strait of Hormuz, and a reported attack on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery. Hormuz tanker traffic is at its lowest rate since May. Asian equities were nonetheless firm on chipmaker strength, with the Nikkei up 2.12% and the Kospi up 4.61%. That cross-asset conflict raises Stress and lowers directional conviction without producing the persistent no-retracement path that defines Tail. The identified structural risk is mechanical: five hours of unpriced escalation headlines clearing into a thin Sunday-style order book at the 22:00Z reopen, which is why the danger window is narrow rather than session-wide. Treasury yields last printed 4.34% at 2 years and 4.77% at 10 years in the Sep 3 H.15 release; no update is published on the holiday. The week's macro risk sits Thursday and Friday with PPI, jobless claims and August CPI.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the last twenty-four hourly Claude assessments are available; the 2026-09-06T21:00Z slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. The window was uniformly green with Tail between 5% and 9% and EA_ON throughout. Stress ran in a 54-62% band, drifting up late as crude extended and the Labor Day holiday thinned participation. Confidence sat at 79-86%. Dominant mode was normal for all but the 14:00Z slot, which was mixed as the energy-versus-equity divergence widened.
outlookSummary: The next twenty-four hours are dominated by market structure rather than macro. Futures halt at 17:00Z and resume at 22:00Z, so five forecast hours carry no tradable price path and Tail sits near its floor. The single elevated slot is the 22:00Z reopen, where five hours of unpriced US-Iran escalation meet the thinnest liquidity of the window; Tail is mapped to WATCH there for one hour only. Path risk then decays through Asian and European hours as depth rebuilds, with a secondary rise into the 13:30Z US cash reopen, the first regular session after the three-day weekend. All post-halt structure is framed conditionally because none of it is observable at the assessment cutoff. The week's principal macro checkpoints, PPI and jobless claims on Thursday and August CPI on Friday, fall outside this window.
